causes_established: The unfolding clip's frame rate was written down twice and the copies disagreed by four percent: ffmpeg assembles at 60 a second (16667 us a frame) while tools/capture/scene.js stepped the driven clock a whole 16 ms between shots, so the sequence fell one frame behind every 400 ms and one shot in every twenty-five re-shot the frame before it. Confirmed against the committed evidence: firing 23's repeats at recorded frames 44, 94, 144, 169, 244, 269 are all in the predicted set 44, 69, 94, 119, 144, 169, 194, 219, 244, 269.
Duration.inMilliseconds truncates an exact run of 16667 us steps to 16, 33, 50, 66, 83 and indexes 0, 1, 3, 3, 4 -- a frame shown twice and a frame never shown, whatever the harness steps by.

The clip's 23-frame head and 21-frame tail were a capture-only 200 ms hold in FoldedNote and a scene asking for 300 frames of a 240-frame fold with a 16-frame settle. Neither is the renders and neither is the decoder.

legibility.py took a run's ink over every mark of that polarity in the ring, so anything darker than the letters became the ink -- which then made on_the_far_side gate the run against a ground lighter than its own false ink, at about one to one, on runs whose ring reading was already 10 to 13.
capture.sh runs neither legibility.py nor palette.py, so both evidence files keep the checkout mtime after a clone and read as firing 23's until someone re-runs them by hand.

measurements.legibility: 25 of 298 below floor -> 16, total_runs unchanged, on_moving_ground 23 -> 14, nine cleared and none created

why_not: IMPLEMENT spans firings and the queue is not drained. Ranks 5 to 9 were deliberately not started: rank 5's residue is the paper material's tooth amplitude, a library re-render, and firings 19, 20 and 22 established that. Rank 10 was taken instead under LOOP section 3c's ruler carve-out.
